image_description: A close-up macro shot of a bright orange coral fungus (Ramaria or Clavulinopsis species). The image focuses on the upper tips of the fungal branches, which are cylindrical and divide into smaller, finger-like projections. The background is a soft, out-of-focus green and brown bokeh, suggesting a forest floor environment. A thin, dark, linear object (likely a pine needle or twig) intersects the right side of the fungal cluster.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic identity of the fungus and ensure it is not a hallucinated hybrid or incorrect class.
To audit the complex boundaries between individual branches and the background, checking for edge bleeding or fusion artifacts common in intricate structures.
To evaluate the naturalness of the depth of field (bokeh) and texture consistency, ensuring the blur looks optical rather than algorithmic.
To verify the spatial separation between the foreground fungus and the background, ensuring no geometric melting occurs at the boundaries.

focus_areas: Branch tip integrity (checking for melting or unnatural smoothing)
Edge sharpness against the bokeh background (checking for haloing/bleeding)
Texture consistency across the cylindrical branches
Naturalness of the intersecting dark twig/pine needle
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the intersection of the dark linear object (twig) with the fungus. In AI images, such intersections often result in depth errors or blending. Verify if the twig sits naturally in front of or behind the branches. Also, scrutinize the tips of the fungus for any 'stumpiness' or lack of fine detail that might indicate generation failure.
